title: One night, 8GB VRAM, 58 looping sprite sheets: the full local pipeline, including what broke
author: RsetX
selftext:
Made a game asset pack end-to-end on consumer hardware — 10 animals, 58 looping

animations — and the interesting part wasn't the generating, it was everything

around it. Posting the whole pipeline because the gotchas cost me more hours

than the GPU did.

**Setup:** RTX 3050 8GB, MiniMax H3 fp8 through ComfyUI, \`--lowvram

\--cache-none\`. Source images were 1024×1024 cartoon illustrations on white.

\## What actually mattered

**Loops close by construction, not by prompting.**

H3 is a \*first-last\*-to-video model. Wire the same LoadImage into both

\`first\_frame\` and \`last\_frame\` and the animation is forced back to its start

pose. I burned several 9-minute generations politely asking the prompt to

"return to the first frame" before noticing the node already solves it. Walk

cycles stopped popping immediately.

**Shrink the subject before generating.**

My sources filled 90%+ of the canvas with \~2% margin. Every time an animal

extended a leg it clipped at the frame edge. Fix: detect the subject bbox,

crop, scale to 80%, recenter on white. Margins went from 1.3–5.9% to 12–16%,

and clipping disappeared entirely. This one is easy to miss because the

\*source\* looks fine — it's the motion that needs the room.

**Length is quantised, and fps isn't a parameter.**

H3 accepts 17k+5 frames only: 5, 22, 39, 56. There's no fps input — it was

trained at 24, so asking for fewer frames gives you \*less motion\*, not slower

playback. If you want a 1-second loop, generate 22 frames AND write a prompt

whose action completes in a second. Otherwise you get half an animation

stretched over the full duration.

**Background removal: don't use the one-click tools.**

rembg/u2net left a soft halo tens of pixels wide on clean line art. What

worked: flood-fill from the borders (never threshold on brightness — a white

sheep gets eaten from the inside), separate shadows by saturation, then

\`binary\_fill\_holes\` to recover eyes and enclosed light areas.

One catch that took a while: \`fill\_holes\` also fills holes that are genuinely

background — the triangle between an arm and a torso, the gap between spread

legs. I now compare each hole's colour against the measured outer background

colour; identical means trapped background, anything with its own tint stays.

Tolerance has to be tight (10/255) or you punch holes in pale subjects.

\---

\## What broke

**WAN 2.2 5B never finished.** Sampling took 2:24, then VAE decode thrashed at

7.93/8GB for 45 minutes and produced nothing. H3's VAE is \~4.9GB and fits;

WAN's didn't, at least not with \`--cache-none\` holding the line. If you're on

8GB, this is worth knowing before you queue 30 jobs.

**My batch script died on a timeout.** During VAE decode ComfyUI's HTTP server

stops answering for tens of seconds. I was only catching \`HTTPError\`, so a

\`TimeoutError\` on \`/history/<job>\` killed a generation that was nearly done.

Catch \`URLError\`/\`TimeoutError\`/\`OSError\` and retry — a timeout means "busy",

not "failed". Give up after N consecutive silences, not on the first one.

If interested in the output you can download it from here: [https://shaddafare.itch.io/shepherds-farm-animated-sprites](https://shaddafare.itch.io/shepherds-farm-animated-sprites)
